item.title: Noise Correlation Spectroscopy: A Review
item.description: arXiv:2610.22392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The frequency noise of an ordinary diode laser, often a nuisance in spectroscopy, can be used to measure atomic coherence. When atoms are prepared in a coherent superposition of two ground states, each random shift in laser frequency changes how much light they absorb, so the transmitted light carries a record of that coherence. Correlating the intensity fluctuations of two fields, each linking one ground state to a shared excited state, reads this record out, a technique known as noise correlation spectroscopy. The correlation signal is narrower than the transparency window the same fields create and switches sign as their frequency difference is tuned. Its width is set by the rate at which the atoms lose coherence and, over a wide range, does not grow with laser power. Over two decades the method has spread from warm vapors to cold atoms, to multi-field schemes, and to diamond and rare-earth-doped crystals. This review, to the author's knowledge the first, brings together its theory, experiments and applications, and examines its limits, the challenges that remain, and the opportunities that could make it a standard spectroscopic tool.
item.dc:creator: Gombojav O. Ariunbold

item.title: Nonrelativistic quantum theory of non-dipole effects in a multielectron atom: radiation transition operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.22527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the work of Hopersky A.N. et al., arXiv: 2609.33494v1 [physics. atom-ph] in the Loudon integral representation, the general analytical structure of the complete operator of a multipole radiation transition taking into account non-dipole effects for a multielectron atom is established. In this Letter this structure is converted to the sum only for all multipoles.
item.dc:creator: Alexey N. Hopersky, Alexey M. Nadolinsky, Rustam V. Koneev

item.title: Two-photon Doppler-free spectroscopy of the $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg transition for quantum sensing in ytterbium
item.description: arXiv:2610.22574v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Here we report atomic structure calculations and experimental observations of the two-photon $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ transition in Yb. The unique level structure of Yb places the $6s6p\;^1P_1$ state's energy at $\approx\!49.7\%$ of the ionization energy, which facilitates two-photon Doppler-free excitation of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg state from the $6s^2\;^1S_0$ ground state at a relatively low optical intensity. This $J= 0 \rightarrow J=0$ transition is immune to first-order Zeeman and electric quadrupole shifts, has reduced sensitivity to higher-order Zeeman shifts, and is further predicted to have relatively low sensitivity to density shifts. Using configuration interaction theory, we compute relevant properties of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ Rydberg state for sensing, including the $C_6$ coefficient, dc polarizability, blackbody radiation (BBR) shift, and BBR depopulation rate. As a first experimental step, we demonstrate two-photon Doppler-free spectroscopy of the $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6s23s\;^1S_0$ transition. From our experimental spectra, we estimate the natural linewidth (lifetime) of the $6s23s\;^1S_0$ state to be 90 kHz (1.8 $\mu$s). We believe this transition, or other $6s^2\;^1S_0 \rightarrow 6sns\;^1S_0$ transitions in Yb with $n\approx23$, may find use in a variety of sensing applications, potentially including a two-photon clock, electrometer, or BBR thermometer.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin D. Hunt, Kyle Beloy, Roger C. Brown, Tobias Bothwell, Harikesh Ranganath, Tanner Grogan, Jacob L. Siegel, Andrew Ludlow

item.title: An improved limit on $^{171}\text{Yb}$ electric dipole moment
item.description: arXiv:2610.22739v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Searches for permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) probe new sources of CP violation beyond the Standard Model. The atomic EDM of $^{171}\text{Yb}$, which is sensitive to its nuclear Schiff moment, is a promising candidate, but previous measurements were limited by noise and systematic effects induced by the optical dipole trap (ODT) that holds the atoms. Here we report a substantially improved search enabled by a dual-ODT configuration with orthogonal polarizations, and spin measurements for precise alignment of static and optical fields. By suppressing the key parity-mixing systematic effect and vector light-shift noise, we achieve a limit of $|d(^{171}\mathrm{Yb})| < 7.5 \times 10^{-28}\ e\cdot\text{cm}$ (95\% C.L.), which represents a 20-fold improvement over the previous work. We also present the first calculation of the nuclear structure factors of the Schiff moment of $^{171}\text{Yb}$. The experimental and theoretical advances combine to tighten constraints on CP-violating pion-nucleon couplings in a global analysis. Moreover, this work demonstrates a pathway toward future measurements in $^{225}\text{Ra}$, where nuclear deformation offers exceptional sensitivity to physics beyond the Standard Model.
item.dc:creator: S. -Z. Wang, S. -B. Wang, E. F. Zhou, Z. -J. Tao, J. -M. Yao, T. Xia, Z. -T. Lu

item.title: Fully relativistic calculation of thermal shifts in spectra of hydrogen molecular ion
item.description: arXiv:2610.22843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Within a fully relativistic framework, we discuss the one-loop self-energy correction, generalized to the presence of external blackbody radiation, for a bound electron in the hydrogen molecular ion. The calculations rely on the thermal part of the photon propagator from finite-temperature quantum electrodynamics. The Dirac equation with a two-center potential is solved using the dual kinetic balance condition, extended to axially symmetric systems, and a B-spline-based trial function. The results are obtained within the Born-Oppenheimer adiabatic approximation. Thermal shift for the ground term of the hydrogen molecular ion is computed as a function of the internuclear distance. Including this correction, we present the resulting shifts of the vibrational levels. The analysis focuses on the dynamical effect, a comparison is made with data available in the current literature.
item.dc:creator: M. A. Reiter, A. A. Anikin, A. A. Kotov, D. A. Glazov, T. A. Zalialiutdinov, D. A. Solovyev

item.title: Resonant pair production and flat band melting in a driven Rydberg chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.22532v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a Rydberg chain subjected to a two-tone periodic drive of the detuning $\Delta(t)$ and Rabi frequency $\Omega(t)$ at frequencies $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2=\nu \omega_1$ respectively with $\nu \in \mathbf{Z}$. In the strong Rydberg blockade limit, such a system reduces to the PXP model and exhibits exact Floquet flat band. Here we determine, using a time-dependent Schrieffer-Wolff transformation, the domain of validity of such PXP dynamics once the blockade-violating processes are taken into account. We study the melting of such flat bands in the presence of strong, but finite, blockade strength. Using Floquet perturbation theory (FPT), we identify two mechanisms for such melting; the first occurs due to the presence of many-body resonances involving resonant production of nearest-neighbor Rydberg excitation pairs while the second involves virtual processes that access intermediate states with such pairs. Our analytical FPT results match with those obtained using exact diagonalization on a finite chain. We study the dynamics for $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ (Fock state with no Rydberg excitation), $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$, and $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ (Fock states with Rydberg excitations on alternate and every third site respectively) initial states. We find that $|{\rm vac}\rangle$ shows exceptional stability against resonant pair formation while $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ exhibits flat band melting via virtual processes away from the direct resonances. We find oscillatory dynamics with large time period for the $|{\mathbb {Z}}_2\rangle$ initial state and the presence of Floquet scars that have large overlap with $|{\mathbb {Z}}_3\rangle$ state; these phenomena occur due to processes that are absent in the PXP limit. We propose measurement of nearest neighbor pair correlation functions using Rydberg atom quantum simulator platforms as an accessible experimental probe for these effects.
item.dc:creator: Tista Banerjee, K. Sengupta

item.title: Universal Threshold Laws for Dipolar Evaporation of Molecular Fermi Gases
item.description: arXiv:2610.22639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fermi statistics suppress the elastic collisions that rethermalize a Fermi gas during evaporative cooling, creating a fundamental low-temperature bottleneck for producing quantum degenerate gases. We show that, for shielded single-component ultracold dipolar molecular Fermi gases in the Wigner threshold regime, this bottleneck is governed by universal threshold laws fixed by the effective dimensionality of the gas. In this regime, Fermi suppression of rethermalization scales quadratically with temperature in 3D but only linearly in 2D. Consequently, the thermalization-to-loss ratio is more favorable in 2D than in 3D, and these results suggest that 2D geometries are better suited for reaching deep degeneracy. We also present ab initio close-coupling calculations that agree well with experimental measurements on Fermi degenerate gases of KRb molecules, supporting our conclusions.
item.dc:creator: Kevin B. Xu, John L. Bohn, Reuben R. W. Wang

item.title: Exponential-SWAP gate between bosonic motional modes of trapped ions
item.description: arXiv:2610.23208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The exponential-SWAP (eSWAP) gate generates a coherent superposition of identity and SWAP operations, with continuously tunable amplitudes. We experimentally implement this gate between two bosonic motional modes of trapped ions using spin-independent and spin-dependent beam splitter interactions. Measurements of selected slices of the joint characteristic function for distinct input states test the gate and demonstrate continuous control of the identity-SWAP superposition. This implementation provides a tunable interaction for hybrid qubit-bosonic quantum information processing.
item.dc:creator: E. J. W. Koh, Rongjie Zhang, Dzmitry Matsukevich

item.title: Precision measurement of the ground-state hyperfine constant for $^9Be^+$ in a linear Paul trap via magnetically insensitive hyperfine transitions
item.description: arXiv:2601.14811v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Direct measurements of the ground-state magnetically insensitive hyperfine transition |F=2,mF=0>->|F=1,mF=0> of $^9Be^+$ ions have been performed using microwave-driven state transfer. The $^9Be^+$ ions are confined and laser-cooled in a linear Paul trap, forming a Coulomb crystal. The transition frequencies have been measured over a magnetic field range of $ \pm 0.5 mT $ centered at zero magnetic field, and the acquired data were fitted accounting for the high-order Zeeman effect. The hyperfine constant A is determined to be -625.008840(35) MHz, achieving a relative precision of $ 5.6 \times 10^{-8}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-yuan Ao, Wen-li Bai, Qian-yu Zhang, Wen-cui Peng, Xin Tong

item.title: A Rydberg atom array coupled to a high-cooperativity optical cavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.20889v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Integrating Rydberg-state control of atom-atom interactions with cavity control of atom-light interactions enables the combination of local entangling operations with photon-mediated long-range coupling, measurement, and communication. Such integration is challenging because electric fields generated by charges on cavity optics and by cavity-stabilizing actuators may disturb Rydberg-state coherence. Here, we couple a Rydberg tweezer array to a high-cooperativity optical cavity, suppressing the electric fields produced by cavity length actuation so that the residual field variation of about $3~\mathrm{mV/cm}$ rms does not limit Rydberg coherence. We demonstrate two capabilities that neither system provides alone. First, we use Purcell-enhanced fluorescence to read out atoms directly in the ground-Rydberg basis within $7.5~\mu\mathrm{s}$, well within the Rydberg-state lifetime, with ground- and Rydberg-state detection infidelities of $3\%$ and $5\%$, respectively, and with low atom loss. Second, we use Rydberg-Rydberg interactions to control collective light-atom scattering into the cavity mode. Specifically, we drive blockaded Rabi oscillations between a state with two ground-state atoms, which scatter collectively with a superradiant or subradiant rate controlled by the atomic positions, and an entangled state with a single Rydberg excitation, which scatters like a single atom. These capabilities open routes toward networked Rydberg processors, mid-circuit measurements in analog quantum simulators, and many-body quantum optics with entangled emitters coupled collectively to light.
item.dc:creator: Tai Xiang, Yue-Hui Lu, Tsai-Chen Lee, Jacquelyn Ho, Michael Lan, Zhenjie Yan, Harry Levine, Nathaniel B. Vilas, Dan M. Stamper-Kurn

item.title: Non-invasive 2D spatial measurements of electric fields within a plasma sheath
item.description: arXiv:2511.12322v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce an all-optical quantum-enhanced diagnostic for electric fields in low-temperature plasmas. Trace amounts of rubidium vapor, added to an argon plasma, allow us to employ spectrally narrow electric field-sensitive optical resonances via the quantum optical effect of Rydberg electromagnetically induced transparency. This non-invasive technique enables measurements of electric fields in plasma with a 1~V/cm precision and a 1.5~V/cm lower detection limit. By collecting the fluorescence from the illuminated region of interest, we reconstruct a 2D spatial profile of the electric field magnitude with $56~\mu$m resolution. As a proof-of-principle demonstration, we measured the changes in the electric field within the plasma sheath surrounding a biased Langmuir probe tip. This method holds significant potential for studying sheath structures in low-temperature plasmas.
item.dc:creator: Mykhailo Vorobiov, Rob Behary, Luke Payne, Nicolas DeStefano, William Torg, Saskia Mordijck, Charles T. Fancher, Neel Malvania, Edward Thomas Jr., Saikat Chakraborty Thakur, Seth Aubin, Eugeniy E. Mikhailov, Irina Novikova
